about: Herbcraft and cooking (docs/PLAYER_SYSTEMS.md §4). Free combination of 1-5 ingredients at a campfire or herb table; scripts/crafting/herbcraft.gd reads this file. Remedies, not wonders: herbs, roots, salt and food doing what herbs, roots, salt and food do.

effect_tags.healing: restores health: effects.healing, points of health
effect_tags.stamina: restores stamina: effects.stamina, points of stamina
effect_tags.warmth: keeps out the cold: effects.warmth_minutes, game minutes
effect_tags.fever: works against the Grey Fever: effects.fever is fever_quiet (with effects.fever_quiet_days) or, for fever-root steeped with white salt, fever_cure
effect_tags.sleep: brings sleep: effects.sleep_minutes, game minutes of heavy sleep
effect_tags.poison: does harm to whoever eats it: effects.poison, points of health lost; poison spoils any remedy it is mixed into

categories.herb: leaves and flowers, steeped or chewed
categories.mushroom: eaten as food; some are deadly
categories.sweet: honey; softens a remedy or a meal
categories.seasoning: common salt and the like; no effect alone, but a meal seasoned well does more
categories.mineral: the white salt of Greystone's deep vein

ingredients.name: Fever-root
ingredients.text: A pale, knotted root dug under the ash trees on the forest path. Steeped strong it quiets the Grey Fever for a few days. Alone it has never cured anyone.

ingredients.name: White salt
ingredients.text: White mineral salt from Greystone's deep vein, the kind no apothecary in the valley sells. Steeped with fever-root it is the old receipt for the Grey Fever.

ingredients.name: Common salt
ingredients.text: Grey cooking salt from the coast, sold by the pound. It does nothing alone; it makes a meal worth more.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.text: Comb honey from the hives behind Maud's hut and the abbey's orchard. It takes the bitterness out of a draught.

ingredients.name: Yarrow
ingredients.text: Soldier's woundwort, white-flowered by the roadside. Bound on a cut it stops the bleeding; steeped it mends.

ingredients.name: Comfrey
ingredients.text: Knitbone. The abbey's herb garden grows it in rows; Maud grows it by her door.

ingredients.name: Willow bark
ingredients.text: Bark stripped from the river willows. Chewed or steeped it eases aches and a hot head.

ingredients.name: River mint
ingredients.text: Water mint from the banks below the ferry. It clears the head and the lungs.

ingredients.name: Watercress
ingredients.text: Peppery cress cut from the shallows at Ferrisford. Bargemen eat it raw by the handful.

ingredients.name: Nettle
ingredients.text: Young nettle tops, picked with a glove. Boiled they lose the sting and keep the strength.

ingredients.name: Ginger root
ingredients.text: A dear root brought up the river to the Lantern Market. One knob warms a man through a winter night.

ingredients.name: Mustard seed
ingredients.text: Brown mustard seed, ground in a mortar. It bites, and the heat stays.

ingredients.name: Garlic
ingredients.text: Cottage-garden garlic. It warms the blood and keeps a stew honest.

ingredients.name: Valerian root
ingredients.text: It smells of old socks and brings sleep like a blow to the head. The monks use it sparingly.

ingredients.name: Hops
ingredients.text: Dried hop cones from the Rusty Nail's brewing. A pillow stuffed with them is a sound night.

ingredients.name: Chamomile
ingredients.text: Little apple-scented daisies. A cup calms a fretful child or a frightened grown one.

ingredients.name: Deathcap
ingredients.text: A pale-green mushroom under the oaks. It tastes of nothing, and the dying starts a day later.

ingredients.name: Nightshade berries
ingredients.text: Glossy black berries on a dull vine. Children are warned off them, and not every child listens.

ingredients.name: Field mushroom
ingredients.text: Pink-gilled mushrooms from the meadows. Good fried; easily mistaken by a careless picker.

ingredients.name: Oats
ingredients.text: Rolled oats from the mill. The base of every pottage in the valley.

ingredients.name: Barley
ingredients.text: Pearl barley. It thickens a stew and keeps a walker walking.

ingredients.name: Turnip
ingredients.text: A poor man's meal, and a filling one.

ingredients.name: Apple
ingredients.text: Sharp russets from the abbey orchard and the valley's cottage trees.

ingredients.name: Mutton
ingredients.text: Salted mutton by the joint. Most of the valley eats meat on feast days only.

ingredients.name: Venison
ingredients.text: Deer meat. In the crown's forests, taking it without leave is poaching.

ingredients.name: Boar meat
ingredients.text: Dark, rich meat from the wild boar of the Darkwood, for whoever lives through the hunt.

ingredients.name: River trout
ingredients.text: Brown trout from the Ferris and the mill race.

ingredients.name: Eel
ingredients.text: Eels from the traps under the River Quarter's wharves. The dockers live on eel pie.

dishes.name: The Grey Fever cure
dishes.text: Fever-root steeped with the white salt of Greystone's deep vein: the old receipt from Brackenmoor's archive. Drunk in full it breaks the Grey Fever for good.
dishes.deed: steeped fever-root with Greystone's white salt and made the true cure for the Grey Fever

dishes.name: Fever-root tea
dishes.text: Fever-root steeped strong. It quiets the Grey Fever for a few days, as root always has. It cures nothing; the fever comes back.

dishes.name: Salt draught
dishes.text: White salt stirred into water. It holds the Grey Fever down for a few days, the way the Hollow's half measures held Elena's. Without fever-root it cures nothing.

dishes.name: Healing draught
dishes.text: A bitter green draught of wound-herbs. It eases pain and helps a body mend.

dishes.name: Rousing tonic
dishes.text: A sharp, cold tonic of river herbs. It puts the wind back in a tired walker.

dishes.name: Warming tonic
dishes.text: A hot, biting tonic. It keeps the cold out for a few hours on the road.

dishes.name: Sleeping draught
dishes.text: A heavy, sour draught. Whoever drinks it sleeps hard and wakes slow.

dishes.name: Bitter draught
dishes.text: A draught that will do harm to whoever drinks it. Any good herb in it is spoiled.

dishes.name: Meat stew
dishes.text: A thick stew of meat and whatever else was to hand.

dishes.name: Fish stew
dishes.text: A river stew of fish, the way the bargemen make it.

dishes.name: Pottage
dishes.text: A pot of grain and greens, the valley's everyday meal.

dishes.name: Stew
dishes.text: It looks and smells like any other stew. It is not.

dishes.name: Dubious food
dishes.text: A grey, doubtful mess. It fills a stomach, barely, and does nothing else.
